title: Tanaris
body: Tanaris is a sea of shifting sand in the far southeast of Kalimdor, south of Thousand Needles and east of Un'Goro Crater. Trolls ruled this land long ago, and the ruins of their old sites still lie half buried among the dunes. Sand trolls of the Sandfury tribe still hold the walled city of Zul'Farrak in the northwest. The goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel have made the rest of the desert their business. Their town of Gadgetzan lives on water drawn from beneath the dunes, yet the Wastewander nomads have seized most of its wells, and Southsea pirates prey on the cartel's ships from a cove on the eastern coast. Older and stranger powers lie deeper in. Silithid hives drain the desert pools, Dunemaul ogres camp among the troll ruins, and in the south great giants walk before the sealed gates of Uldum. In the eastern mountains the bronze dragonflight keeps the Caverns of Time, where the paths of history meet.

title: Gadgetzan
body: Gadgetzan is the chief town of the Steamwheedle Cartel in Kalimdor, a walled goblin settlement among the dunes of northern Tanaris. Like every cartel town it is neutral ground. Anyone with coin is welcome, and the town's bruisers fall hard on whoever starts trouble, asking only whether the culprit really meant to make them hurt someone. Water is the town's lifeblood and its biggest business, managed by the Gadgetzan Water Company, whose officials fret over every well the nomads steal. Around them work alchemists, smiths, engineers and inventors, and the innkeeper sizes up newcomers for the cage matches fought in the town's arena. Flight masters for both the Alliance and the Horde keep their mounts here.

title: Steamwheedle Port
body: Steamwheedle Port is the cartel's harbor on the northeastern coast of Tanaris, linked by road to Gadgetzan, where ships run to and from Booty Bay. Security Chief Bilgewhizzle keeps the peace on its docks. Stoley tends bar and swears by his Steamwheedle bilge rum, thick as gravel and fiery as lava. A haughty fashion designer procures the latest styles for queens and warchiefs, and along the shore a troll mystic named Yeh'kinya and the dwarf Prospector Ironboot pursue their studies, while the gnome soothsayer Narain Soothfancy keeps house just to the north. South of the port waits Torta, a turtle whose husband Tooga went out to fetch dinner and has not found his way home.

title: Noonshade Ruins
body: On the road between Gadgetzan and Steamwheedle Port lie the Noonshade Ruins, a scatter of ancient troll stonework half buried in the sand. Whoever raised them is long gone. The ruins now shelter Wastewander thieves and bandits, who lie in wait among the stones, and starving blisterpaw hyenas and scorpid hunters prowl the dunes around them. Purple lotus grows among the broken walls for those bold enough to pick it.

title: Waterspring Field
body: Waterspring Field, east of Gadgetzan, is the reason the town can survive at all. The goblins raised water towers here to pump the hidden reserves beneath the desert. The Wastewander nomads took the field for themselves, and their rogues, shadow mages and assassins now guard the towers and the wells the Gadgetzan Water Company counts as its own. Their leader, Caliph Scorpidsting, is found here among them, and the Water Company has posted a price on his head for murdering its workers and seizing its property.

title: Lost Rigger Cove
body: Ringed by mountains south of Steamwheedle Port lies Lost Rigger Cove, the hideout of the Southsea pirates. Their walled town has docks and a shipyard, and cargo taken from cartel ships lies about it, including the rum shipment Captain Cuergo stole from Stoley. The cartel pays the pirates protection money, yet lately they ignore the bargain. The pirate Andre Firebeard is wanted for crimes against Steamwheedle and Gadgetzan, and a goblin cutthroat named Kregg Keelhaul is sometimes seen in the cove. A treasure map even claims Cuergo buried a chest of gold on a beach further south.

title: Southbreak Shore
body: South of Lost Rigger Cove the coast opens into Southbreak Shore, a long flat beach washed by the South Seas. Surf gliders, great sea turtles, haul themselves through the shallows, and the beach belongs to giants: coast striders wade along the tide line and a deep dweller lurks in the water beyond. Few travelers linger. On a small island just offshore lives a gnome named Winkey, keeping his own company.

title: Caverns of Time
body: In the mountains of eastern Tanaris a great cavern opens into the realm of Nozdormu, the Timeless One. Here the bronze dragonflight has watched over the flow of time since the world was young, and its guardians bar any who would meddle with it. Before the entrance stands Anachronos, heir of Nozdormu, with his far less welcoming dragonkin companions Tick, Chronalis and Occulus. The Steward of Time greets travelers at the threshold and warns of dangers beyond, then sends them down to the keepers in the depths. Within, tunnels called timeways lead into moments of history that hostile hands are trying to unmake.

title: Broken Pillar
body: South of Gadgetzan a few toppled columns mark the Broken Pillar, the remains of a troll site lost to the sands. Its newest resident is Marvon Rivetseeker, a goblin scholar from Ratchet who crashed his zeppelin nearby and decided to begin his research where he landed. From his camp he studies the troll ruins of the desert and the ornaments of Gahz'ridian the old trolls carved in honor of the hydra Gahz'rilla, and he speaks of what he once saw within the Sunken Temple.

title: Abyssal Sands
body: The Abyssal Sands are the empty heart of Tanaris, a rolling waste of dunes between Gadgetzan and the southern ruins. Little shade and less water can be found here. Fire rocs and their larger kin circle overhead, glasshide basilisks bask on the dunes, and packs of blisterpaw hyenas and scorpids roam the sand in search of prey. Whirling vortexes of wind drift across the waste, and travelers speak of a great firebird that is sometimes seen soaring above it.

title: Sandsorrow Watch
body: West of Gadgetzan, Sandfury trolls guard Sandsorrow Watch, an outpost of watch towers standing over a pool of open water, a rare treasure in the desert. Firecallers, hideskinners and axe throwers patrol its sands, and they do not welcome goblin surveyors. When the Gadgetzan Water Company sent a junior surveyor to sample the pool, some crawling horror ambushed the surveyor there, the first warning of the silithid. A troll called Jin'Zallah the Sandbringer is said to walk among them.

title: Zul'Farrak
body: In the northwest of Tanaris rise the walls of Zul'Farrak, city of the Sandfury trolls, ruthless sand trolls steeped in dark magic who attack anyone who approaches. Warleader Krazzilak prowls before its gates. Legends cling to the place. A hydra god, Gahz'rilla, is said to dwell in a sacred pool within its walls, and the persecutors of the martyr Theka are said to scuttle about his shrine, cursed into scarabs. Many are drawn inside all the same: Sergeant Bly led his band in hunting treasure, the Prophecy of Mosh'aru lies on tablets within, and the smith Trenton Lighthammer of Gadgetzan still remembers with dread the warband that once marched out of it to lay waste to the land.

title: The Noxious Lair
body: On the western edge of Tanaris, above the jungles of Un'Goro Crater, the ground sinks into a broad hollow where pools of water once gathered. They are gone now, drained by the Centipaar silithid who have dug their hive into the sand. Their workers, tunnelers and stingers swarm over the hollow, their eggs lie clustered in the earth, and their sandreavers guard the hive mounds. The Gadgetzan Water Company sent for parts of these bugs, and Alchemist Pestlezugg found them unlike any insect he had ever seen. A great devourer named Soriid is said to hunt among the hives.

title: Dunemaul Compound
body: Not long ago a large band of nomadic Dunemaul ogres wandered into Tanaris and claimed a stretch of desert south of Gadgetzan, building a compound there. Brutes and enforcers guard it, warlocks and ogre mages practice their crude magic, and smaller bands have spread out to occupy the old troll ruins nearby. In Gadgetzan, Andi Lynn fears the force the ogres could build and wants the compound broken before it grows, beginning with its leader, Gor'marok the Ravager. Two rarely seen ogres, Cyclok the Mad and Omgorn the Lost, prowl the camp as well.

title: Eastmoon Ruins
body: West of the Gaping Chasm lie the Eastmoon Ruins, ancient troll stonework slowly swallowed by the dunes. The Dunemaul ogres have spread here from their compound, and their warlocks and ogre mages have made the ruins a camp of their own. Glasshide basilisks and blisterpaw hyenas haunt the edges, purple lotus grows in the shelter of the old walls, and the rarely seen ogre wanderer Omgorn the Lost passes through.

title: Southmoon Ruins
body: North of the Valley of the Watchers stand the Southmoon Ruins, another troll site from the days when trolls held this land. Dunemaul ogres camp among the fallen stones. The ground here is rich in Gahz'ridian, the strange element the old trolls carved into ornaments in honor of their hydra god, and a goblin treasure hunter at the Broken Pillar rewards those who bring him pieces. Searing rocs circle overhead.

title: The Gaping Chasm
body: Southeast of Gadgetzan the desert splits open into the Gaping Chasm, now a hive of the Hazzali silithid. Wasps, swarmers and stingers boil out of its great mounds, while workers and tunnelers dig ever deeper below. Junior Surveyor Scrimshank of the Gadgetzan Water Company was sent here, and his last report spoke of the same strange bugs. He never came back, and only his surveying gear was found. A ravenous silithid called Haarka is feared in the depths, and near the chasm a gnomish homing robot, OOX-17/TN, once crashed and waited for rescue.

title: Thistleshrub Valley
body: In the southwestern corner of Tanaris lies Thistleshrub Valley, a low basin where great cacti grow thick in the heat. Its guardians are living plants: gnarled thistleshrubs and rootshapers that lash out at anything that comes near, and dew collectors that store precious water in special glands. That water has drawn more than one schemer from Gadgetzan. Marin Noggenfogger sought the glands for a drink to quench his thirst, and Tran'rek of Gadgetzan wants a closer look at the valley's cactus, if only someone else will clear the way first.

title: Valley of the Watchers
body: In the far southwest of Tanaris a valley runs between the mountains to a great sealed gate, the entrance to Uldum. Few believe the place behind it is more than a myth. The gate cannot be forced, and huge giants, the Dune Smashers, walk the valley floor as if keeping watch. Scholars of the Explorers' League and the sages of Thunder Bluff have both sent agents here in hope of opening it, and a pedestal before the gate stirs a titan guardian who demands the Plates of Uldum. Prospector Gunstan of the Explorers' League keeps a lonely camp in the valley.

title: Land's End Beach
body: Land's End Beach is the southernmost shore of Tanaris, in the far southeast of Kalimdor, where the desert finally runs out into the South Seas. Surf gliders by the dozen crawl through the breakers. A mermaid named Meridith dwells in the waters here, and she still treasures the day she pulled a gnome from the wreck of his flying machine on this very beach. That gnome was Narain Soothfancy, who had hidden a precious book on a small island further south and crashed on the way home. A pirate's treasure map claims that Captain Cuergo buried his gold on this shore, by a mast, a flag and bones.

title: Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser
body: Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser of the Gadgetzan Water Company hunts for new sources of water now that the nomads hold the wells, and he will hire any likely stranger as a temporary junior-grade surveyor. He dismissed the first reports of water-drinking bugs as nomad trickery, until his own surveyor was ambushed at Sandsorrow Watch and his top assistant, Scrimshank, vanished in the Gaping Chasm. He mourns Scrimshank as a good goblin. Though he dislikes handing out company information for nothing, he trusts his old friend Pestlezugg, and when the alchemist urged it he copied the silithid report for all to read.

title: Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle
body: Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle of the Gadgetzan Water Company is as fierce about profit as he is about justice for the Wastewander nomads who stole his wells. He rewards those who thin the nomads' ranks, pays the company's bounty on their leader Caliph Scorpidsting, and sells off the model 4711-FTZ power sources that once ran the wells, now in surplus thanks to the thieves, reminding buyers that nothing is free in Gadgetzan. He dreams aloud of importing water from the icy springs of Dun Morogh. He also wants back his cherished divino-matic rod, the tool he uses to find new water holes, stolen by a mercenary named Sergeant Bly who led his band into Zul'Farrak.

title: Marin Noggenfogger
body: Marin Noggenfogger is a Gadgetzan goblin with a terrible thirst and a nose for profit. Standing in the desert heat, he hit on the idea of drinking the water stored in the glands of the dew collectors of Thistleshrub Valley. It tasted dreadful, so he turned to his friend Sprinkle, an excellent cook who thinks him a little eccentric, and her secret mushroom powder transformed the brew. The result was the Noggenfogger Elixir, a potion he expects to make millions on. Sprinkle insists he owes her a favor for it. Marin laughs that off as one of her jokes.

title: Curgle Cranklehop
body: Curgle Cranklehop is a Gadgetzan inventor with a soft spot for birds. He is helping the druids save the hippogryphs of Feralas, whose numbers are dwindling under the blight of the Gordunni ogres, and to that end he built the Super Egg-O-Matic, a machine that weighs, measures and packs any hippogryph egg brought to it. He collects eggs of every quality, grieving gently over the ones that cannot be saved, and sends crates of them to Erelas Ambersky in Rut'theran Village to hatch. His latest invention, the Super Snapper FX, takes pictures of anything it is aimed at.

title: Marvon Rivetseeker
body: Marvon Rivetseeker is a goblin scientist from Ratchet and a treasure hunter at heart. He came to Tanaris by zeppelin to study its troll ruins, crashed, and simply began his research where he landed, at the Broken Pillar. He collects the Gahz'ridian ornaments the old trolls carved after the hydra Gahz'rilla, finding them with a detector helmet of his own invention. He once entered the Sunken Temple and barely escaped through its ooze-flooded halls, and he remembers a circular chamber of serpent statues, a trap that nearly killed him, and an altar to Hakkar below. He believes that circle of statues guards a hidden treasure.

title: Yeh'kinya
body: Yeh'kinya is an old troll mystic who lives at Steamwheedle Port, claiming that time and drink have dulled his outer senses but not his inner eyes. He speaks of Hakkar the Soulflayer and the troll prophecy of his return, and claims to want only to keep the god's power from those who would abuse it. With that tale he sent heroes across the world to gather the tablets of Mosh'aru, an ancient egg and at last the essence of Hakkar's avatar. The truth was darker. Yeh'kinya served Hakkar all along, and the egg he guarded helped the Soulflayer return to Zul'Gurub.

title: Prospector Ironboot
body: Prospector Ironboot is an old dwarf scholar who works among the goblins of Steamwheedle Port. Studying the troll legends of Hakkar, he discovered that the prophecy of Mosh'aru was written not on two tablets but on six, and that the troll Yeh'kinya had told only half the tale. Piecing the tablets together, he learned that the egg meant to contain the Soulflayer could instead give him new birth. When his fears came true, Ironboot sent heroes to the Zandalari trolls of Yojamba Isle, who he hoped would know how to defeat the blood god.

title: Narain Soothfancy
body: Narain Soothfancy is a gnome who lives just north of Steamwheedle Port and calls himself a psychic, though his guesses rarely land. A copy of Soothsaying for Dummies sits by his door. He claims a crash on Land's End Beach gave him his super-gnomish powers, and he has a long list of grudges: his ex-best friend forever Stewvul stole his scrying goggles, and his arch-enemy Doctor Weavil once tore his treasured Draconic for Dummies to pieces. Behind the bluster he is a gifted engineer: the blue dragon Azuregos calls him a terrible psychic but an amazing engineer. A mermaid loves him. He insists it could never work.

title: Anachronos
body: Anachronos, heir of Nozdormu the Timeless One, keeps watch before the Caverns of Time in his true dragon form, and he has little trust left for the mortal races. A thousand years ago, when the qiraji fell upon the Caverns during the War of the Shifting Sands, he called the dragonflights to battle and, with Fandral Staghelm and the night elves, sealed the insects behind the Scarab Wall. He forged the Scepter of the Shifting Sands as its key. Fandral shattered it in grief, and Anachronos divided the shards among guardian dragons. Now he insists that this time the first strike must be theirs, so the mistakes of the past are not repeated.

title: Andormu
body: Andormu is a bronze dragon of the Keepers of Time who wears the shape of an elf, at times a grown man and at times a child, both sometimes seen at once. With his sister Nozari he leads the keepers in the Caverns of Time while Nozdormu is away. Small meddlers hardly concern him, such as a greedy wizard nudging the past to better his station. What troubles him now is worse: strange beings seen more and more often across the timeways, trying to alter the course of history itself. The keepers dare not risk themselves, so Andormu welcomes heroes from Azeroth to defend the timeways in their place.

title: Bugs in the Water
body: With the nomads holding its wells, the Gadgetzan Water Company went looking for new water, and Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser sent a temporary junior surveyor to sample the pool by Sandsorrow Watch. The surveyor came back with tales of an ambush by some crawling horror. Fizzledowser had dismissed reports of bugs sucking up the desert's water as nomad mischief. He sent for parts from the Centipaar of the Noxious Lair, where water pools once lay, and Alchemist Pestlezugg found them unlike any insect he knew. Then word came that the surveyor Scrimshank had vanished in the Gaping Chasm, where only his gear was found. Pestlezugg's report was grim: the bugs had been turned into nothing but ravagers by a powerful, malign outside force, a threat to all of southern Kalimdor and perhaps the world. Copies went to scholars in Darnassus and Orgrimmar, who gave the creatures a name: silithid.

title: Wastewander Justice
body: The Wastewander nomads have seized almost every well in Tanaris, and without them Gadgetzan's water will soon run dry. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle of the Gadgetzan Water Company calls it a matter of justice, goblin style. First the bandits and thieves east of town were to be thinned, then the more dangerous rogues, assassins and shadow mages who guard the stolen wells, until the company could take the fight to them. Meanwhile Spigot Operator Luglunket pays a company care package for every handful of water pouches taken from the nomads, since that water was the company's to begin with. Wanted posters in Gadgetzan and Steamwheedle Port name the nomads' leader, Caliph Scorpidsting, for murdering company workers and stealing its resources and property. His death, the company hopes, will finally push the squatters off Gadgetzan's wells.

title: The Noggenfogger Elixir
body: Marin Noggenfogger of Gadgetzan was thirsty, as anyone who stands about in the Tanaris heat must be. He had heard of strange creatures to the southwest, the dew collectors of Thistleshrub Valley, which store water in special glands, and he was sure a drink made from them would quench his thirst. The gland's water tasted dreadful. Rather than give up, Marin sent the dew to his friend Sprinkle, an excellent cook, to give it some kick. Sprinkle knew just the thing: the Violet Tragan, a mushroom that grows only underwater in a lake of the Hinterlands, which she had relied on since childhood to survive her sister's cooking. Ground into a violet powder and mixed with the dew, it produced the Noggenfogger Elixir. Marin, delighted, now plans to make millions. Sprinkle reminds him he owes her a favor.

title: The Southsea Shakedown
body: The Steamwheedle Cartel pays the Southsea pirates of Lost Rigger Cove to leave its ships alone, but lately the pirates have taken the money and kept raiding. The cartel leaned on Security Chief Bilgewhizzle of Steamwheedle Port to teach them a lesson, and since he cannot leave the docks he deputizes whoever will go. A wanted decree authorizes lethal force against the pirate Andre Firebeard, adding that his head may stand in for him at his hearing. One pirate was found carrying the schedules of shipments between the port and Booty Bay, with notes on which ships promise great loot. The port has its own grievances. Captain Cuergo stole Stoley's last shipment of rum just when Stoley needed it to settle a bet with Sea Wolf MacKinley of Booty Bay, and the Haughty Modiste buys up Southsea hats by the score, to be cleaned, personalized and sold to the elite of Azerothian society.

title: The Egg of Hakkar
body: The troll mystic Yeh'kinya of Steamwheedle Port sought the spirits of the vale screechers of Feralas, cousins of an old, old god whose spirits are still linked to him. Once their essence was gathered, he spoke of the troll prophecy that Hakkar the Soulflayer will one day return, and claimed only to want the god's power kept from those who would abuse it. The prophecy of Mosh'aru, he said, told how to contain Hakkar's essence. Its two tablets lay in Zul'Farrak, one with the long-dead martyr Theka, one with the hydromancer Velratha. The tablets spoke of an ancient egg hidden behind the amphitheater atop Jintha'Alor, a relic of the old troll empires. Carried into the Sanctum of the Fallen God within the Sunken Temple, the egg drew in the essence of Hakkar's slain avatar. Yeh'kinya took it, promising to keep it from evil hands.
sources: quests 3520, 3527, 4787, 3528 descriptions and reward texts
notes: Fact-check: verified. Chain starts and ends with Yeh'kinya in Tanaris. 4787 (Hinterlands sort) and 3528 (Sunken Temple sort) are not used by hinterlands.json or swamp_of_sorrows.json. Only 3520 is a trigger. Faction 0.

title: The Lost Tablets of Mosh'aru
body: After the egg of Hakkar passed into Yeh'kinya's hands, the dwarf Prospector Ironboot of Steamwheedle Port came forward with a warning: the troll had not told the truth. There were six tablets of Mosh'aru, not two. The third and fourth were held by the Mossflayer trolls of the Eastern Plaguelands, the fifth and sixth by the Smolderthorn of Blackrock Spire. Reading them together, Ironboot found the hidden half of the legend. The egg was never meant to contain the Soulflayer. It was meant to bring him back. Confronted, Yeh'kinya only gloated that it was too late, for Hakkar was reborn in the ancient troll city of Zul'Gurub, and thanked his dupes for hastening the Soulflayer's return. Ironboot sent them on to Molthor of the Zandalari on Yojamba Isle, whose trolls might know how to defeat the blood god.

title: The Arcanite Buoy
body: When a hero brought Narain Soothfancy a ledger from the blue dragon Azuregos, the gnome learned the dragon wanted an arcanite buoy built, and that the plans were written in Draconic, which Narain cannot read. To begin he needed three things. His scrying goggles had been stolen by his ex-best friend forever, Stewvul, who in turn had lost them in the Molten Core. A five hundred pound chicken came from Dirge Quikcleave of Gadgetzan, who turned the carcass of the chimaerok lord of the Isle of Dread into his Kickin' Chimaerok Chops. Volume two of Draconic for Dummies, hidden on an island south of Land's End Beach, had been booknapped; a ransom drop in Winterspring failed, and Narain's arch-enemy Doctor Weavil scattered the book in eight pieces that had to be found and bound again. At last Narain built the buoy, with a warning about Maws, a hundred feet of death waiting in the Bay of Storms.

title: The Keepers of Time
body: At the threshold of the Caverns of Time the Steward of Time greets travelers he has been expecting and has one of his brothers fly them down to Andormu of the Keepers of Time. A custodian then leads them through the cavern. She explains that the keepers watch over Nozdormu's realm and mend the small disturbances, a rogue mage changing the past to raise his station. The master himself never meddles in mortal affairs and only corrects what others alter, yet he is away now, which means someone is trying to change time on a grand scale. The tunnels around them are timeways, infinite in number, and those open now are trouble spots born of a single disturbance, ranked from least to most catastrophic, though the collapse of any one would end the world. Behind one of them she names a malevolent organization, the Infinite Dragonflight, bent on altering history. There are only two truths here, she says: time is always in flux, and perception does not dictate reality.
